WHAT THE DATA ACTUALLY SHOWS
- The transition sits inside/below the scan: at L=256, P_surv(1000)=1.0 for every lambda 1.71–1.805 (all 16 trajectories survive), and rho(t) at lambda=1.71 is still decaying at t=1000 (rho: 0.375@100 → 0.166@1000, effective tau~1000) — i.e., even lambda=1.71 is at best marginally subcritical on L=256.
- rho_ss at L=256 rises with lambda (0.177 → 0.320), flattening near 1.766–1.785; the three beta-fit lambdas are all supercritical (delta_lambda = 0.03–0.05), but rho_ss is nearly flat there (0.263 → 0.302 → 0.303 size-averaged), which is why beta comes out ~0 with a wide CI.
- 16 seeds quantizes P_surv to 1/16 steps (±0.12 noise), so no estimator pins lambda_c tighter than ~±0.02; the CI reflects that.

ESTIMATOR REFINEMENT MADE DURING IMPLEMENTATION (worth knowing)
My first version used argmax P_surv(1000) per size + 1/L extrapolation; it gave lambda_c=1.702 because at L=128/256 the P_surv curve is a saturated ~1.0 plateau, so the argmax landed on plateau noise at the low end (apparent thresholds trending the wrong way with L). I replaced it with a consistent two-stage per-size rule: (a) argmax P_surv(1000) (tie-broken by slowest late-time decay slope) when the maximum is in an intermediate regime (<0.94); (b) otherwise the first lambda where the flattening ratio rho(1000)/rho(500) ≥ 0.90. This yields the stable values above. The rule is documented in method_summary and the report.

RUNTIME/DEVELOPMENT ISSUES
- Two indexing bugs found and fixed during development (stacked seed-array axis order in the timeseries loop; bootstrap resampling axis) — final code is clean and re-runs deterministically.
- No runtime issues on the final run: 576 trajectories, 27.65M site visits, ~20 s total.

LIMITATIONS (also stated plainly in dp_report.json assessment_note)
- beta and z are weakly constrained under this protocol (16 seeds, t_max=1000, L≤256); dynamic scaling only weakly resolved (R^2=0.631 < 0.8), so universality is not claimed.
- tau_q_half is null because no L=256 P_surv=0.5 crossing exists within t_max.
- delta estimate is noise-dominated (negative value reported as-is, not used in flags).

All contract checks pass: dp_summary.csv and dp_scan.csv (36 rows) and dp_timeseries.csv (36,000 rows) have exactly the mandated columns; dp_report.json has task_id/model/method_summary/evidence/conclusion with all seven explicit evidence subkeys; rho_ss window t=750..1000 used identically at every scan point.
